findings.title: Realized model-pin savings confound model choice with workload volume
findings.what: The implementation reports `baseline.premiumUsd - comparison.premiumUsd` as realized savings even when the periods contain different entry counts, durations, token volumes, or workloads. The test at lines 57-93 explicitly uses one baseline entry versus two comparison entries and asserts subtraction of their unmatched totals. A reduction in traffic alone can therefore produce attributed model-pin savings, while increased traffic can erase genuine per-unit improvement. The derived split repeats the same unsupported total comparison at lines 118-129.
findings.fix: Compare like-for-like normalized premiums, such as premium per input/output token under an explicitly documented normalization, and apply that rate change to a clearly identified comparison workload; alternatively require matched periods/workloads and expose the matching provenance. Update derivation to rank splits using the same normalized measure.
findings.acceptance: Add fixtures with identical model mix but sharply different traffic and verify realized savings is zero, plus fixtures with improved model mix and increased traffic that still reproduce the normalized savings. Assert attribution exposes the normalization basis and source window fields.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed the production subtraction at src/lib/model-pin-savings.ts:181-184, the same unnormalized subtraction in split selection at lines 118-129, and an unequal-entry-count test that deliberately asserts this formula at src/lib/model-pin-savings.test.ts:80-93.

findings.title: Model-pin split inference is quadratic in billable history size
findings.what: For each possible split, the loop allocates two slices, filters the entire suffix, and reduces both prefix and suffix. Across n entries this performs O(n²) work and O(n) transient allocation per candidate after already collecting and sorting the complete unattended history. Large ingestion histories can therefore cause avoidable latency and allocation pressure.
findings.fix: Precompute prefix and suffix counts and premium sums once, then evaluate each boundary in O(1), retaining only the winning index. Slice only once after selection.
findings.acceptance: A benchmark or probe over increasing histories demonstrates near O(n log n) total behavior including sorting, with 2x entries taking materially less than 4x split-evaluation time and without per-candidate array allocations.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read of src/lib/model-pin-savings.ts:107-131 and 210-249 confirmed one initial sort followed by a candidate loop whose `slice`, suffix `filter`, and two `reduce` operations rescan history for every eligible boundary; no prefix/suffix cache exists.
